iconShowsAnimal.definition: The token art shows a whole real-world animal, or the head of one, as a subject: a fish, bird, snake, spider, monkey, octopus, bull or goat. Toys, tracks, tentacles on their own, monster parts and tiny decorative creatures don't count. Borderline, left untagged and scoped out of questions: highpriestess, xaan, pukka, magician, lycanthrope, lleech, lilmonsta, pixie, harpy, golem, kazali.

iconShowsHumanFigure.definition: The token art shows a person-shaped figure with a body (human or ghostly), not just a face, hand or other part. Borderline, left untagged and scoped out of questions: golem.

iconShowsBodyPart.definition: The token art shows a separate part of a body rather than a whole creature: a hand, face, mouth, lips, teeth, eyeball, brain, bone, skull, tentacle or claw, drawn anywhere in the picture. Borderline, left untagged and scoped out of questions: legion, alchemist, goon, oracle, cultleader, fortuneteller, saint, highpriestess, wraith, scapegoat, lordoftyphon, lycanthrope, fearmonger, golem.

iconHasSkull.definition: A skull is drawn somewhere in the token art, including the small skull-and-crossbones on the Alchemist's bottle label. Borderline, left untagged and scoped out of questions: wraith.

iconShowsPlant.definition: A plant or part of one is drawn: a flower, stem, leaf or tree. Borderline, left untagged and scoped out of questions: ravenkeeper, klutz, ogre.

iconShowsFoodOrDrink.definition: The token art shows something to eat or drink, or a vessel that plainly holds it (a pie, a lollipop, a glass of wine, a tankard of beer, a steaming teapot or cup). iconFitsInOneHand.definition: The token art is a small object (or a few small objects) a person could pick up and hold in one hand. Borderline, left untagged and scoped out of questions: every character not in the yes list or that clear-no list, i.e. hats, masks, symbols, small animals, body parts, long tools and weapons, and the like.
